title: Effective Dates and the Waiting Period — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## When coverage attaches under NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

**Standard wait.** *Clause no longer in force:* "New business and every mid-term coverage increase or deductible decrease take effect at 12:01 a.m. on the day that is the tier's standard waiting period in calendar days after the date the signed application (or endorsement request) and the full premium are received." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for new business and mid-term changes. The remainder of the standard-wait sentence stays in force: the waiting days are counted by adding the days to that receipt date on the calendar, and the waiting-period basis recorded is Standard.

**Statutory exceptions.** Two statutory exceptions replace the standard wait, and only one basis is recorded per transaction.

- **Loan transaction** — the coverage is bought or increased in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan secured by the building. The loan-transaction exception applies only when the application and full premium are received no later than the date the loan closes; coverage then takes effect at the loan closing date, the waiting-period basis is Loan Transaction and the loan closing date is recorded.
- **Map revision** — the building was newly placed in a Special Flood Hazard Area by a revision of the Flood Insurance Rate Map. The map-revision exception applies only when the application and full premium are received no later than the tier's map-revision window in calendar months after the map revision that placed the building in a Special Flood Hazard Area takes effect; coverage then takes effect at 12:01 a.m. on the day after receipt (the tier's map-revision waiting period), the waiting-period basis is Map Revision and the map revision date is recorded. The window is counted by adding calendar months to the map revision effective date, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist, and a receipt on the last day of the window qualifies.

*Clause no longer in force:* "When both exceptions could apply, the one giving the earlier effective date is recorded." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Assignment.** An assignment of an in-force policy to the buyer of the building carries no waiting period (the tier's assignment waiting period) and the basis is Assignment.

**Decreases.** Coverage decreases and deductible increases are never effective mid-term; they are accepted only effective on a renewal date.

**Losses before the effective date.** A loss that begins before the effective date of the coverage, or of an increase, is not covered by that coverage or increase.

### The two exception tests at their boundaries

The loan closing date is the one recorded for the transaction, and the map revision date is the one recorded on the policy; the comparison in each case is with the date the application and full premium were received.

| Test | Clock starts | Counting | Qualifies | Does not qualify |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loan transaction | The date the loan closes | Receipt compared with the closing date itself | Receipt on or before the closing day | Receipt on the day after the closing day or later |
| Map revision | The map revision effective date | Add the window's calendar months to that date; if that day does not exist in the month, take the month's last day | Receipt on or before the last day of the window | Receipt on the day after the last day of the window or later |

*Hypothetical boundary cases (abstract dates).*
- A loan closes on a given day and the application and full premium arrive that same day: the loan-transaction exception applies and coverage takes effect at the loan closing date. Had they arrived the day after, the exception would not apply.
- A map revision takes effect on the 31st of a month, and the month reached by adding the window's months has only 30 days: the window ends on the 30th of that month. A receipt on that 30th qualifies; a receipt on the following day does not.
